benefits: Rescues washed-out or backlit photos by spreading tones across the full brightness range.
Area mode fixes just the dark subject — the sky and background stay untouched.

Real histogram equalization math, the same technique taught in image-processing courses.

faqs.a: Histogram equalization redistributes brightness levels so they use the full 0–255 range. It builds a histogram of tones, computes the cumulative distribution, and remaps each tone. Dark, flat photos gain punchy contrast because crowded tones get spread apart.

Luminance mode equalizes overall brightness while preserving the original colors — best for photos. RGB mode equalizes each color channel separately, which can shift colors dramatically (a blue cast may turn orange). Try luminance first.
faqs.q: Luminance or RGB mode — which should I pick?

faqs.a: Switch to Area mode, drag a box around the dark subject, and only those pixels are equalized. The rest of the photo is left exactly as it was.
faqs.q: Can I equalize just part of the image?

faqs.a: Equalization amplifies everything, including JPEG noise and grain in shadows. If the result looks gritty, the original had heavy noise in the dark areas — a mild denoise before equalizing helps.
faqs.q: Why does my photo look noisy after equalizing?

faqs.a: Equalization stretches tones apart, which can create visible banding in smooth gradients like skies. The area mode helps: equalize only the subject, not the sky.
faqs.q: Why do I see bands in the sky?

photo-equalizer.formula:
histogram h(v) = count of pixels with tone v
cdf(v) = sum of h(0..v)
new(v) = round((cdf(v) - cdfMin) / (N - cdfMin) x 255)
Example: 4 pixels with grays [50, 50, 100, 200]
cdf: 50->2, 100->3, 200->4; cdfMin = 2
map(50) = 0, map(100) = 128, map(200) = 255.
howTo: Upload a photo from your device (up to 15 MB).
Choose Full for the whole image or Area, then drag a box over the region to fix.
Pick Luminance for natural contrast or RGB for dramatic per-channel equalization.
Tick the compare box to flip between original and equalized versions.
Press Download to save the equalized image as a PNG.
keyFacts: Histogram equalization spreads the image's tones across the full 0–255 brightness range for maximum contrast.
Two scopes: Full (whole image) and Area (drag a box — only those pixels change).
Two channel modes: Luminance (preserves colors) and RGB (equalizes each channel, stronger color shifts).
A compare checkbox flips the preview between the original and the equalized version.
Computed per pixel with the Canvas API — the photo never leaves your browser.
The download is a lossless PNG, rendered at up to 1400 px on the long edge.

limitations: Rendering is capped at 1400 px on the long edge, so huge originals are scaled down first.
Equalization amplifies noise and JPEG artifacts in dark areas — it cannot distinguish noise from detail.
Smooth gradients (skies) may show banding after aggressive equalization.
It cannot recover detail that was clipped to pure black or pure white in the original.

photo-equalizer.workedExample:
A 4-pixel row has grays [50, 50, 100, 200].
Histogram: 50 appears twice, 100 once, 200 once; cdfMin = 2.
map(50) = (2-2)/(4-2) x 255 = 0; map(100) = (3-2)/2 x 255 = 128; map(200) = 255.
The flat row becomes [0, 0, 128, 255] — full contrast from the same data.
